dabs.address: 73 W 7200 S, Midvale, UT 84047

summary.t: A family-owned Midvale brewery that grew from a home-brew kit into a big 21+ taproom with its own beer store.

makes.t: Brian Coleman started home brewing in 2010; he and DeDe Coleman run the brewery, which now brews more than 50 beers a year.
Its beer is also sold in state liquor stores and poured at some bars and restaurants.

visit.t: The taproom at 73 W 7200 S opened in November 2023 in a former ax-throwing range: a full bar, a kitchen, a stage, pool tables and indoor cornhole courts, with the brewhouse in view.
It is 21 and over.

toGo.t: Every beer is sold cold from the on-site beer store, including high-point cans and growler fills, seven days a week.

locals.t: City Weekly readers placed its Huckleberry Sour Ale second for best sour beer in 2025.
A City Cast Salt Lake reader called it arguably the best brewery in the state and good value, writing before the taproom opened.

trib2024.title: 2 Row Brewing brings a 'brewery experience' and regulation-size cornhole courts to Midvale

places.name: Main Street bar and package agency

summary.t: Park City gin specialists, with a Main Street lounge and award-winning botanical spirits.

makes.t: Run by Rob and Sara Sergent since 2016; Sara Sergent was inducted into the London Gin Guild, and its Elevated Gin won a Gin of the Year gold in London.
Says it is the only U.S. maker whose whole botanical lineup is vapor-extracted; it also makes whiskey, vodka and liqueurs.

visit.t: The Main Street lounge serves cocktails and local pies and offers guided tastings and custom gin-making; both locations are 21+.

toGo.t: Both the Main Street lounge and the Silver Creek distillery have a package agency selling its bottles.

dabs.address: 2245 S West Temple, Salt Lake City, UT 84106

summary.t: The Salt Lake distillery behind Jack Rabbit Gin, started by three friends in 2013.

makes.t: Three friends started distilling in 2013; the lineup includes Jack Rabbit Gin, barrel-aged gins, vodka, rum, rye and a four-year bourbon grown, distilled and aged in Utah.
Salt Lake Magazine credits it as the first Utah distiller to make canned cocktails, such as a mule and a gin rickey.

visit.t: It closed its bar in 2024 but kept distilling.

toGo.t: Some bottles, like the four-year bourbon, are sold at the distillery; most of the range is in Utah state liquor stores.

locals.t: City Weekly readers voted Jack Rabbit Gin the best local gin of 2025.

dabs.address: 445 S 400 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84047

summary.t: A downtown Salt Lake brewpub from two home-brew shop owners, built around British pub beers, German lagers and house-made sausages.

makes.t: Founded by Cody McKendrick and Ross Metzger, who also owned Salt City Brew Supply; it opened in December 2019 planning traditional British pub beers and German lagers plus fruited and experimental taps.
Says it is Independent and Craft Malt Certified, with part of its malt grown regionally and malted locally.

visit.t: Licensed as a bar, so it is 21+ with ID scanned at the door; no dogs, including on the patio (licensed service dogs excepted).
A small kitchen focuses on handmade sausages and sandwiches; there are dart boards, and no scheduled tours, though staff may show you the brewhouse if someone is free.
Parties of seven or more should call ahead.

toGo.t: Cans, crowlers and growlers to go.

locals.t: City Weekly readers voted its Big Crispy West Coast Pilsner the best lager or pilsner of 2025 and put its ESB second for best ale.

ksl2019.title: At Bewilder, home-brew entrepreneurs bring passion for beer to downtown digs

places.name: Bottle shop and package agency (temporary space)

summary.t: A Salt Lake City whiskey brand making bourbon and rye, now with a tiny bottle shop in its temporary home while it looks for a permanent one.

makes.t: Started by three Utah-raised childhood friends, Jeremy Rawle, Jay Williams and Matthew Seegmiller; at its 2017 launch the bourbon came from Indiana allotments, was bottled in Houston and was run from a Salt Lake City headquarters.
The lineup is an American bourbon, an American rye and a limited-release straight rye, all 86 proof, aged in new American white oak and cut to proof with Wasatch snowmelt water.
The bourbon is a blend of two straight bourbons and took a Double Gold at the 2018 San Francisco World Spirits Competition.

visit.t: The bottle shop is small and stocks the whiskeys plus merch; the company calls the Pickett Circle space temporary.

toGo.t: Bottles are sold at the shop, where DABS lists a package agency (PA-604), the kind DABS says lets a distillery sell the bottled spirits it produces.
Its where-to-buy list names many Utah state liquor stores, from Logan to St. George, plus a handful of bars and restaurants.

locals.t: SLUG Magazine's 2017 profile pitched it as an affordable premium whiskey from hometown friends, already poured at Salt Lake spots like HSL, Manoli's and Water Witch.

summary.t: A brewery in Moroni, in Sanpete County, licensed by DABS in June 2024.

makes.t: Blue Hills Brewery came before the DABS commission as a new brewery applicant on June 27, 2024, and its beer manufacturing license dates from that day.

dabsJun2024.title: Utah Department of Alcoholic Beverage Services Commission Meeting (agenda)

dabs.address: 94 E 7200 S, Midvale, UT 84047

summary.t: A Midvale restaurant-brewery opened by Czech immigrants in 2001, known for Central European lagers and food like bratwurst, pierogies and goulash.

makes.t: Joe and Helen Petras opened it in 2001 to bring the food and beer of their native Czechoslovakia to Utah; Joe chose to brew lagers, which take longer to make than ales.
Since 2018 it has been owned by the group behind Porcupine Pub and Grille, The Dodo and the Rio Grande Cafe, who said they would keep the restaurant and the Czech beers.

visit.t: A full restaurant: the menu the Tribune singled out includes bratwurst, pierogies and goulash.

locals.t: City Weekly readers placed its Czech Pilsner second for best lager in 2025, and the brewery third for best brewery food and second for best German restaurant.
A City Cast Salt Lake reader said it makes the best beer in Utah and praised the food.

trib2018.title: Midvale's Bohemian Brewery, famous for Czech beer and brats, gets new owners

dabs.address: 1315 N Horsemans Park Dr., Dammeron Valley, UT 84783

summary.t: An estate winery north of St. George, making wine from its own Dammeron Valley vineyard.

makes.t: Vineyard owner Mark Bold partnered with John Delaney, a sommelier and part-owner of St. George's Painted Pony, to found the winery; in 2019 the 12-acre vineyard had about 9,000 vines of 11 varieties.
DABS lists wines including Viognier, Verdejo, Malvasia, Grenache, Tempranillo, Petite Syrah and an estate Pinot Noir.

sgn2019.title: Bold and Delaney Winery and tasting room to open at Dammeron Valley Vineyards

dabs.address: 1641 N Main St., Tooele, UT 84074

summary.t: A Tooele restaurant and brewery making classic ales and lagers since 2012, with motorsports names and a view toward the Great Salt Lake.

makes.t: Brewing since 2012 in small batches of about 300 gallons, with most malt from a small maltster in Idaho Falls.
The lineup leans on classic styles: an amber, an Irish-style red, a nitro dry Irish stout, a wheat ale and seasonals, plus house sodas.

visit.t: The Restaurant and Pub at 1641 N Main St. serves pub food and mixed drinks alongside the beer.
Its beer is also poured at every Pins & Ales bowling center (Tooele, West Valley, Draper and West Jordan).

locals.t: City Weekly named it the best exurban brewery of 2025, for its patio with the Great Salt Lake on the horizon.

dabs.address: 205 W 29th St., Ogden, UT 84401

summary.t: A Latino-owned Ogden brewery making Mexican-style cerveza artesanal, founded by Javier Chávez Jr.

makes.t: Describes itself as a Latino-owned craft brewery dedicated to Mexican-style craft beer.
Founder and brewer Javier Chávez Jr. grew up in Ogden in a family restaurant business; in 2020 he brewed a Mexican-style lager with Cerveza Cabrito in Monterrey, Mexico.

ubn2020.title: Zólupez Beer Company honors Mexican culture, traditions

dabs.address: 4391 S Enterprise Dr., St. George, UT 84790

summary.t: A St. George winery growing grapes on the slopes of Pine Valley Mountain, poured at Silver Reef.

makes.t: Makes small lots from grapes grown at a vineyard on Pine Valley Mountain; DABS lists its Terra 5047 wines, including a Super Tuscan-style blend, Cabernet Sauvignon and rosé.

visit.t: Its wines are poured at the St. George Beverage Co. / Silver Reef restaurant, which shares its DABS address.

dabs.address: 2285 S Main St, South Salt Lake, UT 84115

summary.t: A small South Salt Lake taproom brewing modern American-style ales.

makes.t: Brews what it calls boldly crafted, modern American-style ales.

visit.t: The taproom on South Main is pitched as a cozy third space; call ahead for group events.

toGo.t: A small retail corner sells canned beer to go.

dabs.address: 564 W 700 S, Ste. 401, Pleasant Grove, UT 84062

summary.t: Utah County's first legal distillery, known for small, unusual batch spirits.

makes.t: Matt and Stephanie Eau Claire opened it in March 2020; early releases were Lorenz, a cinnamon-twist rum, and Josephine, an unaged fruit brandy distilled with rum.

visit.t: The tasting room hosts regular tastings and cigar pairings from a walk-in humidor.

toGo.t: When it opened, the distillery was the only place in Utah to buy its bottles; several are now on state store shelves.

locals.t: City Weekly readers placed it third for best distillery tour in 2025, with its vodka second, Sophie's Gin third and Lorenz third in their categories.

trib2020.title: Utah County's first distillery takes the unconventional route

dabs.address: 2617 UT-32 Kamas, UT 84036

summary.t: A Kamas cidery, opened in 2025, making bone-dry mountain ciders from cider-apple varieties.

makes.t: Brendan and Carly Coyle opened it in 2025; their orchard sits at 6,440 feet.
All its ciders are dry with zero residual sugar; the flagship Dry Cut '24 blends 15 apple varieties from three partner orchards in the Mountain West.

dabs.address: 3100 S Washington St., South Salt Lake City, UT 84115

summary.t: A South Salt Lake distillery built on an artesian well, making whiskey, vodka, gin and rum.

makes.t: Its spirits are made with water from an artesian well on land once owned by Hugh Moon, an early Utah distiller.
The range covers vodka, gin, rum and a line of straight rye whiskeys, some sold only at the distillery.

visit.t: Tours with a five-spirit tasting, or a tasting only, by reservation; it also offers a whiskey program where you buy and follow your own barrel.

toGo.t: Several cask-finished ryes are sold only at the distillery.

locals.t: City Weekly readers placed Dented Brick Premium Rum second for best local rum in 2025.

dabs.address: 273 Trolley Square, Salt Lake City, UT 84102

summary.t: The brewpub at Trolley Square, brewing since 1995, with a full menu and a beer store.

makes.t: Began brewing in 1995 and says its Happy Valley Hefeweizen won Utah's first Great American Beer Festival gold medal.
Leans a little hoppier than most: the canned lineup runs from a Mexican-style lager and hefeweizen to West Coast and hazy IPAs.

visit.t: A full-service pub with lunch and dinner menus and Sunday brunch, including kids' dishes; enter through the mall entrance.

toGo.t: A beer store at the pub sells cold beer to go seven days a week.

home.title: Desert Edge Brewery (home, menus and beer store)

dabs.address: 2374 S Redwood Rd., Salt Lake City, UT 84119

summary.t: The small, self-financed maker of Brigham Rum, named for Utah's deciding vote to end Prohibition.

makes.t: Owned and run by Creed Law, Jensen Dobbs and Jon Gregersen, who built their own still; its award-winning Brigham Rum is made from sugar cane.
The name honors Utah as the 36th state to ratify the 21st Amendment, the vote that repealed Prohibition in December 1933.

dabs.address: 7321 S Canyon Centre Pkwy., Cottonwood Heights, UT 84121

summary.t: A distillery with a full restaurant in Cottonwood Heights and a 21+ lounge downtown.

makes.t: Spirits include Devil's Gate Bourbon, Ragtown American Whiskey and Green Ditch Gin; it says the whiskey and bourbon it distilled from scratch will be ready in 2027, and compares its current bottlings to dishes built in-house from bought ingredients.

visit.t: The Cottonwood Heights restaurant has a restaurant license, so the main dining room is family-friendly; the upstairs lounge and the downtown lounge are 21+.

toGo.t: Sealed bottles are sold on site under its distillery retail license, including Sundays and holidays.

locals.t: City Weekly readers ranked it second-best restaurant in Salt Lake County for 2025 and third for restaurant views.

dabs.address: 825 S State St., Salt Lake City, UT 84111

summary.t: The Salt Lake brewery that bet on strong beer first, best known for its barrel-aged Big Bad Baptist imperial stout.

makes.t: Opened in 2009 as Utah's first brewery since Prohibition to brew only high-alcohol beer, back when Utah capped grocery and draft beer at 4%.
Known for the Big Bad Baptist barrel-aged imperial stout series, released in a new version each year; the range runs from Los Locos Mexican-style lager to IPAs and strong Belgian-style ales.

visit.t: The tasting room pours 2-ounce samples of every beer in its fridge, which usually holds 50 or more beers.

toGo.t: After tasting you can buy beer to take home, including six-packs.

locals.t: City Weekly readers placed Big Bad Baptist third for best stout in 2025.

dabs.address: 700 W SR 24, Torrey, UT 84775

summary.t: Utah's first orchard-based cidery, in Torrey near Capitol Reef, making ciders and session meads.

makes.t: Grows fruit in its Torrey orchards (including high-tannin cider apples like Kingston Black and Dabinett) and buys from local farmers; it also makes session meads.

visit.t: The taproom pours flights of cider and mead; tours of the production space run 30 to 60 minutes and can be booked.
It is licensed as a bar, so it is 21+ only; dogs are allowed on the patio but not inside.

toGo.t: A bottle shop at the taproom.

dabs.address: 320 W 800 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84101

summary.t: A revived 1884 Salt Lake brand, now an employee-owned Granary District taproom with ever-rotating ales and lagers.

makes.t: Fisher was founded in 1884 as one of Utah's first breweries and has returned as an employee-owned craft brewery.
Pours small-batch ales and lagers that rotate constantly.

visit.t: The taproom has a dog-friendly patio and food trucks on a weekly schedule; it is open seven days a week.

toGo.t: Fresh beer to go from the taproom.

locals.t: City Weekly readers voted it the best brewery of 2025, and second for best dog-friendly bar patio, beer selection and can art.

dabs.address: 333 W 2100 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84115

summary.t: A brewery and restaurant in a former bank on 2100 South, known for beer, wine-hybrid seltzers and a vegan-friendly menu.

makes.t: Opened in April 2020 in a building that had been a bank and then a tile store; founders Drew Reynolds, Justin Belliveau and brewer Jeremy Gross started planning it in 2014.
Besides beer it makes seltzers built on white and red grape juice, including a high-point aperitif seltzer.

visit.t: The menu was planned to be vegan-friendly; readers also point to its rooftop patio.

locals.t: City Weekly readers voted it the best hard seltzer of 2025 and placed Grid City Pilsner third for best lager.
A City Cast Salt Lake reader recommended it for groups with mixed tastes, citing the seltzers and the rooftop.

dabs.address: 501 N Main St., Heber City, UT 84032

summary.t: A small Heber City taproom with a constantly changing tap list and occasional high-point can releases.

makes.t: Taps change constantly, so it suggests calling ahead; the list has included a German-inspired lager and an annual imperial stout aged in High West whiskey barrels.
When it has spare fermentation space it cans small runs of high-point (over 5%) beers, announced on social media.

visit.t: Drink in the small taproom on Main Street.

toGo.t: Beer to go from the taproom.

summary.t: Carbon County's own brewery, with pizza, on Helper's Main Street.

makes.t: Amy and Jaron Anderson moved to Helper in 2018 and opened the brewery in April 2023, part of the town's revival.
Jaron Anderson trained under Kevin Templin of Templin Family Brewing.

visit.t: A brewery with a pizza kitchen.

summary.t: Utah's first legal distillery since 1870, best known for blended whiskeys like Rendezvous Rye and American Prairie Bourbon.

makes.t: Founded in 2006 by David and Jane Perkins with a 250-gallon still and a saloon in a historic Park City livery stable.
Known for blended American whiskeys; DABS lists its bottles under Constellation Brands as the vendor.

visit.t: Tours of the Wanship distillery run Wednesday to Sunday; reservations are strongly recommended and guests take a shuttle from the lower lot.
The Saloon on Park Avenue is a restaurant and bar in Old Town Park City.

locals.t: City Weekly readers voted it the best distillery of 2025 and the best restaurant view in Park City, and ranked it second-best Park City bar and distillery tour.

summary.t: A Logan cidery named for its owners' rescue dogs, using apples from their own Cache Valley orchard.

makes.t: Ben and Lori began fermenting at home in 2002 and bought a 10-acre farm in Paradise, Utah, in 2014 to grow their own cider apples.
Makes ciders from more than a dozen apple varieties, some from that farm.

visit.t: Tasting flights at the Logan cidery; 21+ only.

toGo.t: Bottles to take home from the cidery.

dabs.address: 207 W 4860 S, Murray, UT 84107

summary.t: A Murray distillery with a nautical theme, making navy-strength gin, absinthe, shochu and vodka.

makes.t: Co-owned by Barbie Busch DeShazo, Michael DeShazo and head distiller Ethan Miller, who previously blended at High West and was head distiller at Dented Brick.
DABS lists its Bosun's Navy Gin, Cerulea Gin, Apparition Absinthe, Tsunami Shochu and Perla Vodka.

summary.t: A downtown Logan taproom in a 1903 building, brewing small rotating batches with Cache Valley grain.

makes.t: Co-owners Chris Sisneros-Kidd (brewer) and Cullen Williams opened in May 2025; the brewery uses malted grain grown in Cache Valley.
A small on-site brewhouse keeps a rotating list of new styles and classics.

visit.t: A tavern-style room in the historic building, restored with its original floors and neon sign.

toGo.t: To-go packs from the beer fridge, or 32-ounce crowlers filled from the tap.

trib2025.title: Home Range Brewing opens in downtown Logan

dabs.address: 1048 E 2100 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84106

summary.t: A Sugar House brewpub started by a neighborhood native, with a rotating tap list and a full food menu.

makes.t: Opened in 2018 by Sugar House native Chad Hopkins; the house beers rotate and the menu leans on local ingredients.
Recent taps include an annual pumpkin-pie chocolate stout and lagers made with locally malted grain.

visit.t: Licensed as a bar, so it is 21+ and you don't have to order food; there is live music and a brunch menu.
Also pours local spirits, ciders, coffee and kombucha.

locals.t: City Weekly readers placed it third for best brewpub in 2025.

summary.t: A downtown Cedar City winery and tasting room, near the Utah Shakespeare Festival.

makes.t: Owner and winemaker Doug McCombs opened Iron Gate Winery in 2012; wines are made and blended in Cedar City from grapes grown in California, Oregon, Washington and Utah.

visit.t: White, red, mixed and reserve tasting flights with no reservation needed, plus a by-appointment barrel-room tasting; it also serves cocktails.

summary.t: A Granary District brewery known for its sours and cream ale, with a tavern, a can shop and pinball.

makes.t: Owned by Andrew Dasenbrock; the beer list includes sours, among them a gluten-free grapefruit cherry sour.

visit.t: The tavern is open seven days a week, with warehouse seating and cornhole on Friday and Saturday nights.
Readers point to the pinball machines in the Granary District room.

toGo.t: A can shop sells beer to go seven days a week.

locals.t: City Weekly readers voted its Coffee Cream Ale the best ale and its Blackberry Sour the best sour beer of 2025.

summary.t: The French restaurant at the mouth of Little Cottonwood Canyon, with its own vineyard and estate wines.

makes.t: Makes Château La Caille estate wines from its own vineyard, plus wines from grapes sourced in California and Washington.

visit.t: Wine and cheese pairings (five wines with Caputo's cheeses) on Fridays, by reservation.

toGo.t: Château La Caille wine is sold only at the winery and restaurant.

locals.t: City Weekly named La Caille Utah's best French restaurant of 2025.

dabs.address: 2496 S West Temple St., South Salt Lake City, UT 84115

summary.t: A South Salt Lake brewery with wood-fired pizza, best known for hazy IPAs and lagers, now with a second downtown taproom.

makes.t: Owner Mark Medura began as a home brewer; the brewery made its first beers in 2018 near the South Salt Lake water tower.
Year-round cans run from a Belgian-style blonde to hazy pale ales, with an annual limited Red Feather series.

visit.t: At the original brewery you can tour the brewhouse, eat wood-fired pizza and hear live music on the patio; guests must be 21+ with ID.
The newer Post District taproom downtown has a bigger pizza oven and a patio.

toGo.t: Both locations have a store for beer to go.

locals.t: City Weekly readers voted it the best brewpub of 2025, second for brewery food and third for beer selection.
A City Cast Salt Lake reader called it the top brewery in the city, singling out the Suss It Out IPA and the pizza.

dabs.address: 686 S Main St., Moab, UT 84532
686 S Main St., Moab, UT 84532

summary.t: Moab's brewpub since 1996, which also distills vodka, gin and single-malt whiskey and sells them from its own package agency.

makes.t: Founded in 1996; beers range from an American lager and a pilsner to IPAs and an oatmeal stout, and several have won medals, including a 2014 Great American Beer Festival bronze.
The distillery makes Class 5 Vodka, Spot On and Tight Squeeze gins and Canyonlands Confluence single-malt whiskey, and imports Rayo agave spirits from Mexico under its own label.

visit.t: A big scratch-kitchen restaurant aimed at people coming off the trails and rivers, open daily.

toGo.t: Its package agency sells bottles to go daily, including Sundays and most holidays, when state stores are closed.

summary.t: A veteran-owned meadery in Grantsville, one of the few in Utah.

makes.t: Makes meads (honey wine), including a cold brew coffee mead made with a veteran-owned local company.

visit.t: Offers tastings and special events.

toGo.t: Utah buyers pick up at the meadery or special-order through DABS for delivery to a state store.

dabs.address: 425 N 400 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84103

summary.t: Utah's original craft cidery, making dry ciders and perry in Salt Lake City.

makes.t: Calls itself Utah's original craft cidery; the range includes an English-style dry cider, a dry-hopped cider, fruit ciders and an imperial perry.
City Weekly notes six year-round cans and seasonals such as a winter wassail cider.

locals.t: City Weekly readers voted it the best hard cider of 2025 and ranked it second-best cidery.

places.name: Winery and tasting room at Mt. Naomi Farms

summary.t: Cache Valley's first winery, on the Meikle family's Mt. Naomi Farms in Hyde Park, making wine only from grapes grown on the farm.

makes.t: Every bottle comes from the farm's own vines, about 22 grape varieties; the summer 2026 tasting menu had 11 wines: five reds, five whites and a rosé.

The winery says its vineyard sits near 5,000 feet; its pours include whites such as Chardonel, Riesling and Grüner Veltliner, and reds such as Cabernet Franc and its signature Chump blend, named for a family joke about Keith Meikle's father.
Keith Meikle, who took a two-year winemaking program at UC Davis, is the head winemaker; Brenda Meikle runs the business side.
The Meikles spent about three years pushing Cache County to allow farm wineries as a way to keep their land in farming; the county passed its first alcohol ordinance in 2021.
Keith Meikle made wine in a home winery for years; the commercial winery was finished in 2025, and that year's harvest was its first public release.

visit.t: The tasting room sits behind the farm's red barn, which is also a wedding venue; the winery offers tasting flights and a guided tour of the vineyard and production space.
The farm also runs a U-pick berry patch and the Vineyards at Mt. Naomi event venue.

toGo.t: Since September 2025 the winery has held a DABS package agency on site, the Type 5 kind that lets a maker sell the bottles it produces.
Wine club members pick up their bottles at the tasting room.

locals.t: The Herald Journal reported that the winery found warm support from neighbors and Cache Valley businesses, despite a culturally dry valley and some friction with local government.

summary.t: An Ogden Valley distillery near the ski resorts, making Utah's only locally made agave spirits.

makes.t: Founded in December 2016 by Chris Cross, a former Navy pilot, and Ashley Cross.
Distills spirits from blue agave (including a vodka), Oomaw Gin, a tart-cherry liqueur, apple brandy and a bourbon fermented and aged on site.

visit.t: A 90-minute tour led by the founder, and tastings; ID required. Ski boots are welcome.

toGo.t: Bottles are sold at the distillery, and some (a barrel-rested gin and the bourbon) only there.

dabs.address: 1755 Bonanza Dr. Unit C, Park City, UT 84060

summary.t: A Park City brewery known for low-alcohol hoppy beers that have won Great American Beer Festival gold.

makes.t: Founder Conor Brown specializes in low-ABV hoppy beers; Offset lists three Great American Beer Festival gold medals, two of them for session IPAs.

visit.t: 21+ only (no babies either), but well-behaved dogs are welcome; snacks include local Bavarian-style pretzels and tinned fish, and you can bring your own food.
Its website lists the Forestdale Drive address; DABS still lists an older Bonanza Drive address.

toGo.t: Cans to go.

locals.t: A City Cast Salt Lake reader said its beer rivals favorite breweries around the country.

dabs.address: 358 Park Blvd., Ogden UT, 84401
358 Park Blvd., Ogden UT, 84401

summary.t: An Ogden brewpub by the Ogden River with American food, Mexican-style lagers and a riverside patio.

makes.t: Opened at the start of 2023 in the former Ogden River Brewing space, run by Lane Montoya and Brian Zinsmann of Wimpy and Fritz with brewer Jacquie King, formerly of Roosters.
The tap list leans on lagers, including a Mexican lager it says won World Beer Cup gold in 2026, plus a tangerine wheat ale and IPAs.
DABS also lists Becker's Premium Lager at this address and links it to Ogden Beer Co.'s website.

visit.t: A full restaurant with burgers, sandwiches and cocktails; the riverside patio welcomes kids and dogs, and the upstairs patio is 21+.

toGo.t: Growler and crowler fills of any beer on tap, plus cans to go.

se2023.title: Ogden Beer Co. launches, takes over ex-Ogden River Brewing space

dabs.address: 615 W Stockman Way, Ogden, UT 84401

summary.t: The locally owned company that runs the Squatters Pubs restaurants and brews its own beer at the downtown Salt Lake City pub.

makes.t: When Monster Beverage bought the Squatters and Wasatch beer brands in 2022, the restaurants and brewpubs were left out; a local group led by Squatters founders Peter Cole and Jeff Polychronis then bought Salt Lake Brewing Co., the company that runs them.
Under that deal the pubs kept pouring Squatters and Wasatch beers, buying them from Monster.

In March 2023 the company took over the 10-barrel brewhouse next to the downtown pub and brought back longtime Squatters brewmaster Jason Stock; his first beer for Salt Lake Brewing Co. was Dog Lake Pale Ale.
By late 2025 the pubs poured in-house beers by Stock and by Nils Imboden, alongside popular beers from the Squatters and Wasatch lineup.

The Squatters Craft Beers and Wasatch Brewery brands still belong to Monster, which closed their Salt Lake City brewery in May 2025 and moved production to its other breweries; the pubs, a separate company, were not affected.

visit.t: In late 2025 the company put all its locations, including the former Wasatch brewpubs, under one name: Squatters Pubs.
The downtown pub opened in 1989 as Salt Lake City's first brewpub, and guests can watch beer being brewed.

Other Squatters Pubs are in Sugar House (the former Wasatch brewpub on Highland Drive), West Valley City (opened in 2025 as Squatters Corner Pub), the Roadhouse in Park City, the Craft Café near the airport, and Concourses A and B at Salt Lake City International Airport.
The Top of Main brew pub on Park City's Main Street, where Wasatch opened in 1986, closed for good in spring 2026 as the building's owner moved to sell it.

toGo.t: After the 2022 sale the pubs stopped selling beer to go, because a brewery package agency requires brewing on site and the brewing had gone to Monster.

DABS lists a beer manufacturing license and a package agency for the company at the downtown pub since February 2023, plus an off-premise beer retailer license there; we couldn't confirm what it sells to go.

locals.t: City Weekly readers voted Squatters Pub Brewery the best brewery food of 2025 and second-best brewpub.

summary.t: A religious organization based in a pyramid in Salt Lake City that makes sacramental wines, which it calls nectars, for its own religious practice; they are not sold.

makes.t: Summum was incorporated in Utah in 1975 as a nonprofit that teaches its philosophy, and it received the first wine manufacturing license Utah issued, in 1981.
Its nectars are made inside the pyramid from what Summum describes as an ancient pre-Egyptian formula: they rest for 77 days, then age for one to fifteen years.
Summum calls each nectar a "publication" because, in its teaching, the wine carries spiritual concepts; it says it has made nine of a planned 27.
The nectars are meant as a sacrament for Summum's meditation practice, with a small amount drunk just before meditating.

toGo.t: There is nothing to buy: Summum told the Tribune it does not sell wine and may use it only in its religious practice.
Summum says the nectars are available only to people who have learned its beginning meditation.

locals.t: The Salt Lake Tribune looked into why a pyramid in the Poplar Grove neighborhood holds a wine license, and explained it as a religious sacrament, much as other faiths use wine.

summary.t: A fantasy-tavern cidery and meadery in Salt Lake City's Central Ninth neighborhood that makes its own ciders and meads and pours them in its taproom.

The cider and mead list rotates with the seasons and with whatever the makers want to try next.

summary.t: The brewpub at the entrance to Zion National Park, with canyon views and scratch-made pub food.

makes.t: Handcrafted ales poured at its own pubs and at bars and restaurants in St. George, Springdale and around Utah.

visit.t: The Brew Pub just south of the park entrance serves lunch and dinner seven days a week; the attached Tavern serves drinks without food. A second spot, Station II, is a taproom and bar in downtown St. George.

toGo.t: A growler bar at the Springdale brew pub.

summary.t: A Leeds vineyard and tasting room among the sandstone hills, founded by Michael Jackson.

makes.t: Founder Michael Jackson came to wine through travel in California wine country while in the Navy, and later settled in the St. George area to grow grapes.

visit.t: Offers tastings and vineyard tours, and has hosted wine yoga.
